instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires registration when a person receives compensation/reimbursement of "more than an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter" to communicate with legislative/executive branch members.
The statute requires registration when a person "makes a total expenditure of an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter" on lobbying activities.

The statute exempts from registration any person who spends "not more than 26 hours, or another amount of time determined by the commission" during a calendar quarter engaging in lobbying activity, establishing a time-based threshold in the lobbyist definition.

Detailed per-item itemization (name of beneficiary, description, amount category) is only required when a gift, award, or memento exceeds $50; below that amount, individual itemization is not required, establishing a $50 itemization de minimis threshold.

Texas exempts persons from registration (and thus from filing any disclosure) entirely if expenditures/compensation fall at or below $200 per calendar quarter; this is the only dollar-based filing-exemption threshold in the statute.

Texas uses an absolute hours threshold (26 hours per calendar quarter) rather than a percentage of an individual's compensated time, so no percentage-of-time filing-exemption threshold is defined in the statute.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell based on the Texas statute text.

**Row 001**: §305.003(a)(2) sets compensation threshold at "more than an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter."

**Row 002**: §305.003(a)(1) sets expenditure threshold at "an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter."

**Row 003**: §305.003(b-3) creates a time-based exemption: a person is not required to register if they spend "not more than 26 hours" per calendar quarter on lobbying activity. So time standard exists at 26 hours/quarter.

**Row 004**: Itemization thresholds in §305.0061: detailed reporting required when expenditures exceed 60% of legislative per diem for transportation/lodging/food/entertainment, or exceed $50 for gifts/awards/mementos. The $50 gift threshold is the clearest per-item itemization threshold.

**Row 005**: No overall de minimis exemption from filing based on total expenditures — the $200/quarter is the registration trigger, not an exemption. Once registered, all reportable expenditures must be reported.

**Row 006**: §305.003(b-3) uses an hours-based test (26 hours/quarter), not a percentage of compensated time.
